The owl search found no matches across 18 files, and no mascot appears in any screenshot. What a patient sees in the chapter 1 panels (guide-en-desktop.png, guide-en-phone.png and the es/zh-Hans pairs) is the surgical site and anatomy: the mastoid head dressing, hands lifting it off, the incision behind the ear with its closure strips, and a magnified ear panel labeled 'Check for tape' / 'Revise si hay cinta' / '检查有没有胶布'.

One narrator voice per narrated language and no character: the voices fact lists a single voice (George) for en, es and zh-Hans, and nothing in the screenshots speaks in a character's persona; the transcripts address the patient directly ('Two days after surgery, remove the mastoid dressing'). Worth saying plainly to Song: the same voice id is used for all three languages, and audio is not something a screenshot can judge, so the Spanish and Mandarin delivery still needs a listen by a native speaker before this counts as settled.

Captions exist for all seven segments in en, es and zh-Hans. At 1280x800 the caption bar sits under the picture with the spoken word highlighted ('after' in guide-en-desktop.png, 'después' in guide-es-desktop.png, '天后，' in guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png) and a Captions / Subtítulos / 字幕 checkbox is visible and on. At 375x812 the transcript under the player is the caption track and highlights the same spoken word in bold with a rule beside it (guide-en-phone.png, guide-es-phone.png, guide-zh-Hans-phone.png); text is large and unclipped at that width.

Seven chapters are listed and every one is visible without scrolling at 1280x800 in all three languages (left rail in guide-en-desktop.png, guide-es-desktop.png, guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png, each row with its title and length). Every seek landed exactly on its chapter start (0, 12.4, 37.44, 61.92, 77.68, 101.28, 129.36 s) and set the matching active chapter. At phone width the list becomes a labeled chapter control, 'CHAPTER 1 OF 7' with the chapter title, a dropdown chevron and prev/next buttons (guide-en-phone.png), which a patient can find.

Switching language changes page, audio and captions together. Spanish loads /assets/audio/v2/es/bandage-off.mp3 and the expected first sentence; Mandarin loads the zh-Hans audio and its expected first sentence. The screenshots show no English left behind: guide-es-desktop.png is Spanish throughout (Idioma, Imprimir la tarjeta, chapter titles, TRANSCRIPCIÓN, Reproducir, Subtítulos, LLAME PARA PEDIR AYUDA), and guide-zh-Hans-desktop.png likewise (语言, 打印卡片, 文字稿, 播放, 字幕, 打电话求助). The phone views match.

Paste to link measured 20 ms, with no network requests after load and no account or login field, so a provider stays in the text file and opens nothing new. provider-filled.png shows the four columns with the provider's override and where it came from: Antibiotic No, Pain medication Yes, Follow-up 10/01/2026, Language Español, each marked 'your block', plus the Reviewed by row. provider-draft.png shows the same table against the unfilled dot phrase: every row keeps its preset ('Use the draft default (Yes)', 'Use “about two weeks”', 'Use the draft default (English)') and says in plain words why it will not read a *** placeholder as an answer. The link carries the choices (#a=0&p=1&f=2026-10-01&l=es) and guide-from-link.png opens in Spanish with 'Su revisión de la herida y examen del oído: 1 de octubre de 2026' in the transcript.

The review is one line in the block, 'Video guide: language {English/Spanish/Mandarin}    Reviewed by *** on ***', and the page tells the truth about it. provider-filled.png says 'Not shown to the patient, and not carried in the link. It stays in your note.'; the link fragment carries no review date, and guide-from-link-badges.png, scrolled to the end of the transcript, shows chapter 7 running out with no reviewer line or badge. That matches the 2026-09-19 decision to keep the reviewer in the provider's note.

The card is one tap away at both widths and serves (HTTP 200). 'Print the card' sits in the header at 1280x800 (guide-en-desktop.png, and translated in the es and zh-Hans desktop shots).
